## Input Files

```{r}
resolve_existing_path <- function(candidates) {
  existing <- candidates[file.exists(candidates)]
  if (length(existing) == 0) {
    stop(
      "Could not find the power output directory. Checked:\n",
      paste(candidates, collapse = "\n")
    )
  }
  existing[[1]]
}

# Power_Output/ holds the SLURM run of 2026-05-11, which predates GRAPHS, ATLAA
# and SWSD. Power_Output_2026-08/ is the local re-run that includes them. Listed
# first so the fresh run wins where it exists, with the May run as a fallback.
power_dir <- resolve_existing_path(c(
  "../../../Output/Paper1_Output_Submission2/Power_Output_2026-08",
  "Output/Paper1_Output_Submission2/Power_Output_2026-08",
  "../../../Output/Paper1_Output_Submission2/Power_Output",
  "Output/Paper1_Output_Submission2/Power_Output"
))
message("power_dir = ", normalizePath(power_dir, mustWork = FALSE))

power_results_file <- file.path(power_dir, "targeted_quantile_power_results.csv")
screening_results_file <- file.path(power_dir, "targeted_quantile_power_screening.csv")
summary_file <- file.path(power_dir, "targeted_quantile_power_collection_summary.csv")
missing_tasks_file <- file.path(power_dir, "targeted_quantile_power_missing_tasks.csv")
mapping_file <- resolve_existing_path(c(
  "../../../Input/Harmonized_Datasets/Targeted_Analyte_Category_Mapping.csv",
  "../../Input/Harmonized_Datasets/Targeted_Analyte_Category_Mapping.csv",
  "../Input/Harmonized_Datasets/Targeted_Analyte_Category_Mapping.csv",
  "Input/Harmonized_Datasets/Targeted_Analyte_Category_Mapping.csv"
))

power_results <- readr::read_csv(power_results_file, show_col_types = FALSE)
screening_results <- readr::read_csv(screening_results_file, show_col_types = FALSE)
collection_summary <- readr::read_csv(summary_file, show_col_types = FALSE)
analyte_mapping <- readr::read_csv(mapping_file, show_col_types = FALSE) %>%
  distinct(Code, Category)
missing_tasks <- if (file.exists(missing_tasks_file)) {
  readr::read_csv(missing_tasks_file, show_col_types = FALSE)
} else {
  tibble()
}

power_results <- power_results %>%
  left_join(analyte_mapping, by = c("analyte" = "Code")) %>%
  mutate(
    tau = factor(tau, levels = sort(unique(tau))),
    analysis = recode(
      analysis,
      within_study_demographics = "Within-study demographics",
      pooled_study = "Pooled study"
    ),
    panel = recode(str_to_title(panel), Maternal = "Adult"),
    Category = replace_na(Category, "Unmapped")
  )

screening_results <- screening_results %>%
  left_join(analyte_mapping, by = c("analyte" = "Code")) %>%
  mutate(
    analysis = recode(
      analysis,
      within_study_demographics = "Within-study demographics",
      pooled_study = "Pooled study"
    ),
    panel = recode(str_to_title(panel), Maternal = "Adult"),
    Category = replace_na(Category, "Unmapped")
  )

analysis_palette <- c(
  "Within-study demographics" = "#0F4C5C",
  "Pooled study" = "#D17A22"
)

panel_palette <- stats::setNames(
  as.character(paletteer::paletteer_d("ggsci::default_igv")[1:2]),
  c("Child", "Adult")
)

category_levels <- power_results %>%
  distinct(Category) %>%
  arrange(Category) %>%
  pull(Category)

category_palette_base <- c(
  "FlameRetardants" = "#FFD23F",
  "Flame_Retardant" = "#FFD23F",
  "PAH" = "#6C8FD9",
  "Parabens" = "#9AA3AD",
  "PCB" = "#D7B07A",
  "PCBs" = "#D7B07A",
  "Pesticides" = "#FF6B3A",
  "Pesticide" = "#FF6B3A",
  "PFAS" = "#D8E58A",
  "Phenols" = "#2D8FD5",
  "Phthalates" = "#F45A2A",
  "TraceElements" = "#69C3EC",
  "Trace_Elements" = "#69C3EC",
  "Smoking" = "#4C8A2B",
  "VOC" = "#4B0D57",
  "VOCs" = "#4B0D57"
)

category_palette_fallback <- stats::setNames(
  rep(as.character(paletteer::paletteer_d("ggsci::springfield_simpsons")), length.out = length(category_levels)),
  category_levels
)

category_palette <- category_palette_fallback
matched_categories <- intersect(names(category_palette_base), category_levels)
category_palette[matched_categories] <- category_palette_base[matched_categories]

power_theme <- function() {
  theme_minimal(base_size = 12) +
    theme(
      plot.title = element_text(face = "bold", size = 15, color = "#14213D"),
      plot.subtitle = element_text(size = 10.5, color = "#4F5D75"),
      axis.title = element_text(face = "bold", color = "#14213D"),
      axis.text = element_text(color = "#2B2D42"),
      strip.text = element_text(face = "bold", color = "#14213D"),
      panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
      panel.grid.major.x = element_line(color = "#E6E8EF", linewidth = 0.3),
      panel.grid.major.y = element_line(color = "#D9DEE8", linewidth = 0.35),
      legend.position = "bottom",
      legend.title = element_text(face = "bold"),
      legend.background = element_rect(fill = "transparent", colour = NA)
    )
}

study_power_dist <- power_results %>%
  filter(study != "Pooled") %>%
  group_by(panel, analysis, study) %>%
  summarise(
    models = n(),
    median_power = median(power, na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

category_power_dist <- power_results %>%
  group_by(panel, analysis, Category) %>%
  summarise(
    models = n(),
    median_power = median(power, na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

power_by_covariate <- power_results %>%
  mutate(covariates_used = replace_na(covariates_used, "")) %>%
  tidyr::separate_rows(covariates_used, sep = ";") %>%
  mutate(
    covariates_used = stringr::str_trim(covariates_used),
    covariate_type = dplyr::case_when(
      covariates_used == "" ~ NA_character_,
      covariates_used %in% c("Child_Age", "Mat_Age") ~ "Age",
      covariates_used %in% c("Child_Sex", "Adult_Sex") ~ "Sex",
      covariates_used %in% c("Mat_Race", "Child_Race", "Mat_Child_Comb_Race") ~ "Race",
      covariates_used %in% c("Mat_Edu", "Edu_Any", "Mat_Edu_Binary") ~ "Education",
      covariates_used %in% c("Mat_Income", "Mat_Income_Binary", "Family_Income_Cont") ~ "Income",
      covariates_used %in% c("Sample_Collection_Year", "Year") ~ "Time",
      covariates_used %in% c("Study", "Location", "Location_Region", "Center", "Location_Country", "Site_Location", "State", "Country") ~ "Geography/Study",
      TRUE ~ "Other"
    )
  ) %>%
  filter(!is.na(covariate_type)) %>%
  distinct(task_id, analyte, tau, panel, analysis, study, covariate_type, power, observed_p, n)
```

## Plot 1: Power Distribution by Tau

```{r}
p_power_hist <- power_results %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = power, fill = analysis)) +
  geom_histogram(bins = 28, alpha = 0.78, position = "identity", color = "white", linewidth = 0.2) +
  facet_grid(panel ~ tau) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = analysis_palette) +
  scale_x_continuous(limits = c(0, 1), labels = label_percent(accuracy = 1)) +
  labs(
    title = "Distribution of Estimated Power",
    subtitle = "Power estimates across quantiles for within-study and pooled models",
    x = "Estimated power",
    y = "Number of models",
    fill = "Analysis"
  ) +
  power_theme()

p_power_hist
```

## Plot 4: Top Studies by Median Power

```{r}
# Study-panels where every simulation failed come through with median_power NA.
# slice_max keeps them and fct_reorder below then errors on the NA level, which
# takes down the whole document. Drop them here and say how many, rather than
# letting a silent NA decide what the figure shows.
n_all_na <- sum(is.na(study_power_dist$median_power))
if (n_all_na > 0)
  message("power figure: dropping ", n_all_na,
          " study-panel(s) with no successful simulations: ",
          paste(unique(study_power_dist$study[is.na(study_power_dist$median_power)]),
                collapse = ", "))

study_power_tbl <- study_power_dist %>%
  filter(!is.na(median_power)) %>%
  group_by(panel, analysis) %>%
  slice_max(order_by = median_power, n = 15, with_ties = FALSE) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  mutate(study = as.character(study))

p_top_studies <- study_power_tbl %>%
  mutate(study = forcats::fct_reorder(study, median_power)) %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = study, y = median_power, fill = analysis)) +
  geom_col(position = position_dodge(width = 0.72), width = 0.66, color = "white", linewidth = 0.15) +
  coord_flip() +
  facet_wrap(~ panel, scales = "free_y") +
  scale_fill_manual(values = analysis_palette) +
  scale_y_continuous(limits = c(0, 1), labels = label_percent(accuracy = 1)) +
  labs(
    title = "Studies with Highest Median Power",
    subtitle = "Top studies ranked within each panel and analysis family",
    x = NULL,
    y = "Median power",
    fill = "Analysis"
  ) +
  power_theme()

p_top_studies
```

## Plot 5: Histogram of Power Per Study

```{r}
# Same guard as Plot 4: a study whose simulations all failed has an NA median
# and fct_reorder cannot place it, which aborts the knit.
all_studies_hist <- power_results %>%
  filter(study != "Pooled") %>%
  group_by(study) %>%
  mutate(study_median_power = median(power, na.rm = TRUE)) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  filter(!is.na(study_median_power)) %>%
  mutate(study = forcats::fct_reorder(as.character(study), study_median_power))

p_power_hist_by_study <- power_results %>%
  filter(study != "Pooled") %>%
  mutate(study = as.character(study)) %>%
  left_join(
    all_studies_hist %>% mutate(study = as.character(study)) %>%
      distinct(study, study_median_power),
    by = "study"
  ) %>%
  # The join brings back the all-NA studies that all_studies_hist dropped, so
  # filter again on this side before ordering.
  filter(!is.na(study_median_power)) %>%
  mutate(study = forcats::fct_reorder(study, study_median_power)) %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = power, fill = analysis)) +
  geom_histogram(bins = 24, alpha = 0.82, position = "identity", color = "white", linewidth = 0.2) +
  facet_wrap(~ study, scales = "free_y", ncol = 6) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = analysis_palette) +
  scale_x_continuous(limits = c(0, 1), labels = label_percent(accuracy = 1)) +
  labs(
    title = "Power Distribution Within Studies",
    subtitle = "All within-study cohorts, ordered by overall median power",
    x = "Estimated power",
    y = "Number of models",
    fill = "Analysis"
  ) +
  power_theme()

p_power_hist_by_study
```

## Suggested Supplementary Figure Panel

```{r fig.width=16, fig.height=20}
supp_fig_a <- power_results %>%
  group_by(panel, analysis, tau) %>%
  summarise(
    median_power = median(power, na.rm = TRUE),
    q25 = quantile(power, 0.25, na.rm = TRUE),
    q75 = quantile(power, 0.75, na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = tau, y = median_power, color = analysis, group = analysis, fill = analysis)) +
  geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = q25, ymax = q75), alpha = 0.14, linewidth = 0, show.legend = FALSE) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 1.2) +
  geom_point(size = 2.7) +
  facet_wrap(~ panel) +
  scale_color_manual(values = analysis_palette) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = analysis_palette) +
  scale_y_continuous(limits = c(0, 1), labels = label_percent(accuracy = 1)) +
  labs(
    title = "A. Median power across quantiles",
    x = "Tau",
    y = "Median power",
    color = "Analysis"
  ) +
  power_theme()

supp_fig_b <- power_results %>%
  filter(study != "Pooled") %>%
  mutate(study = as.character(study)) %>%
  left_join(
    all_studies_hist %>% mutate(study = as.character(study)) %>%
      distinct(study, study_median_power),
    by = "study"
  ) %>%
  # As above: drop study-panels with no successful simulations before ordering.
  # This is the S9B panel, so those cohorts are absent from the published figure.
  filter(!is.na(study_median_power)) %>%
  mutate(study = forcats::fct_reorder(study, study_median_power)) %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = power, fill = analysis)) +
  geom_histogram(bins = 22, alpha = 0.8, position = "identity", color = "white", linewidth = 0.2) +
  facet_wrap(~ study, scales = "free_y", ncol = 6) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = analysis_palette) +
  scale_x_continuous(limits = c(0, 1), labels = label_percent(accuracy = 1)) +
  labs(
    title = "B. Study-specific power distributions",
    x = "Estimated power",
    y = "Models",
    fill = "Analysis"
  ) +
  power_theme()

supp_fig_c <- power_results %>%
  group_by(panel, analysis, Category) %>%
  summarise(
    median_power = median(power, na.rm = TRUE),
    models = n(),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  filter(Category %in% top_categories_hist$Category) %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = median_power, y = forcats::fct_reorder(Category, median_power), fill = Category)) +
  geom_col(width = 0.64, color = "white", linewidth = 0.15) +
  facet_grid(panel ~ analysis) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = category_palette, guide = "none") +
  scale_x_continuous(limits = c(0, 1), labels = label_percent(accuracy = 1)) +
  labs(
    title = "C. Category-level median power",
    x = "Median power",
    y = NULL
  ) +
  power_theme()

supp_fig_d <- power_results %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = n, y = power, color = panel)) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.18, size = 1.2) +
  geom_smooth(se = FALSE, linewidth = 1.0, method = "loess", span = 0.9) +
  facet_wrap(~ analysis) +
  scale_color_manual(values = panel_palette) +
  scale_y_continuous(limits = c(0, 1), labels = label_percent(accuracy = 1)) +
  labs(
    title = "D. Sample size versus power",
    x = "Model sample size",
    y = "Estimated power",
    color = "Panel"
  ) +
  power_theme()

supp_patchwork <- (
  supp_fig_a /
    supp_fig_b 
    #(p_covariate_power + p_category_hist)
) +
  plot_annotation(
    title = "Power characteristics of targeted censored quantile models",
    theme = theme(
      plot.title = element_text(face = "bold", size = 17, color = "#14213D"),
      plot.subtitle = element_text(size = 11, color = "#4F5D75")
    )
  ) &
  theme(legend.position = "bottom")


supp_patchwork <- supp_patchwork + plot_layout(guides = "collect", heights = c(0.7, 1.3))


ggsave(
  filename = "../../../Output/Paper1_Output_Submission2/Plots/Final_Patchplots/Wihtin_Cohort_Power_Patchplot.pdf",
  plot = supp_patchwork,
  device = "pdf",
  height = 16,
  width = 12
)
```

```{r}
 power_results %>%
  filter(study != "Pooled") %>% 
  group_by(study,panel,analysis) %>% 
  summarise(
    median_power = median(power, na.rm = TRUE),
    iqr_power = IQR(power,na.rm = T),
    q25 = quantile(power, 0.25, na.rm = TRUE),
    q75 = quantile(power, 0.75, na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>% 
  dplyr::mutate(power_over_90 = ifelse(median_power > 0.9,1,0)) %>% 
  count(power_over_90, name = "n_studies") %>% 
  kable(digits = 3)
```
